newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus jails four Americans for police assault.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus jails four Americans for police assault.

text.p: A court in Cyprus on Friday jailed three American basketball players and a U.S. marine for up to 14 months for attacking a local policeman who told them not to bother his girlfriend.

Players Kip Stone, 25 and Anthony Reed, 24, were jailed for 14 months, while the same district court jailed U.S. embassy marine Christopher Wallace, 25, and basketball player Randy Davis, 27, to 12 months in jail.
All four had pleaded guilty to charges of causing bodily harm to a Greek Cypriot police officer during a night-time brawl at a cafe in the capital Nicosia in March.
The policeman, attacked with tables and chairs and kicked repeatedly in the head, was in a coma for about a week after the incident.
State prosecutors withdrew charges of damage to property and injuring another two policemen who intervened. Charges against a fifth American were withdrawn.

"The law gives us a 10-day period to file an appeal," said Christos Triantafyllides, one of the defence lawyers. "We shall decide whether to appeal or not after we have studied the judgement issued by the court."

Stone, a player in the ENAD team, Reed, a player for APOEL, and Davis, a player for AEK -- all local first division teams -- had been in Cyprus for about a year before the incident. Wallace had been there for seven months.
